profile.entities: JSW Cement Limited (Parent); JSW Steel Fujairah FZE (JV)
profile.subseg: Grey Cement; GGBS (Ground Granulated Blast Furnace Slag); Ready-Mix Concrete (RMC)
profile.themes: Northern India Expansion; Cost Deflation via Green Energy; GGBS Supply Chain Disruption; Geopolitical Fuel Risks

bull_bear.body: Dividend recommended INR 0.50/share based on Adjusted PAT of INR 668 Cr. Focus on deleveraging post-major Nagaur capex; no immediate M&A; potential JV buyout in UAE in 2-3 years.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical tension in West Asia impacting fuel/packing bag costs; Regulatory delays for Punjab plant (EC approval); Labor shortages in key Southern states; GGBS slag supply dependency on JSW Steel contracts.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Optimistic on long-term demand and North India traction; Prudent on accounting (expensing launch costs); Nimble regarding capacity reallocation (Rajasthan vs. Punjab); Confident in cost leadership via ESG/green energy.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly expensed INR 23 Cr North India launch costs rather than capitalizing them to adhere to 'prudent accounting,' artificially depressing Q4 margins despite minimal revenue contribution from Nagaur in the quarter. The Punjab plant delay has triggered a strategic pivot to double down on Rajasthan grinding capacity (6 MT total) rather than waiting, utilizing existing limestone reserves for potential future clinker lines there.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Long-term credit rating upgraded to IND AA- (from IND A+, Stable outlook) by India Ratings and Research.
- Net Debt/EBITDA (TTM) and Net Debt/Equity both improved sharply from a year earlier, indicating a deleveraging balance sheet even as the large capex program (up to 68.3 MTPA grinding potential) continues to ramp.
- Deck does not disclose an explicit dividend policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Cement Volume: 2.35 MT (+12% YoY), Realization INR 4,673/ton (+4.8% QoQ); GGBS Volume: 1.57 MT (+5.4% YoY, impacted by Dolvi slag availability), Realization INR 3,682/ton; RMC Revenue: INR 184 Cr (Q4). Trade mix improved to 51%.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Slag availability constraints at Dolvi unit impacted GGBS volumes by ~1.2 lakh tons in Q4. | UltraTech Cement | beneficiary | Med | Competitors with stable slag supply or integrated steel operations may capture short-term GGBS market share in Western India during JSW's supply realignment. |
| High freight costs and geopolitical tension making imported slag/clinker expensive for peers. | JSW Cement | beneficiary | High | JSW's fixed-price clinker tie-up from Japan (pre-war) and captive UAE JV provide a significant cost advantage over peers relying on spot market imports for their coastal grinding units. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Part of JSW Group, a ~US$25bn Indian conglomerate spanning steel, energy, ports, paints and mobility, providing raw material, power, logistics and brand synergies plus customer trust.
- Among India's fastest-growing cement manufacturers with a multi-region footprint across South, West, East and North India, plus UAE.
- India's single largest manufacturer of GGBS, with ~84% all-India GGBS market share, 9,800+ active dealers and 7,500+ direct customers.
- Lowest CO2 emission intensity in the Indian cement industry (268 kg/ton, FY26), 52% below Indian peers and 50% below global peers.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Corporate] CCPS financial instruments were converted to equity shares prior to the company's IPO, per a footnote on an exceptional fair-value item.
- [Sector Outlook] CRISIL-sourced demand CAGR (FY26-31P) by segment: Rural housing 7.5-8.5%, Urban housing 5.5-6.5%, Infrastructure 8.5-9.5%, Industrial & Commercial 7.0-8.0%, with GGBS demand expected to grow faster than cement demand.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 EBITDA/ton INR 916 (INR 950 adjusted for forex). Cost savings roadmap: INR 100/ton total expected (INR 69-70 power, INR 36 logistics, INR 4 premiumization) by FY28. Green energy mix to rise from 24% (FY26) to 63% (FY27). Fuel cost stable at INR 1.49/Kcal.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Volume Growth: Mid-to-high teens for FY27 (excluding North); North Plant Utilization: 50-60% for FY27; Capex: INR 2,300 Cr (FY27), INR 2,200 Cr (FY28); Margin Trajectory: Improving via INR 100/ton cost savings over FY27-FY28.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Not applicable for cement sector; demand visibility tied to infrastructure/housing projects in South & West India, with new pipeline developing in Rajasthan/Haryana.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Nagaur expansion: Additional 2.5 MT grinding capacity approved (total 6 MT by Q4 FY28) to offset Punjab delays; UAE grinding unit commissioning delayed to April 2027; Potential second clinker line in Rajasthan pending Punjab EC status.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: JSW Cement successfully commissioned its strategic Nagaur plant in March 2026, marking entry into North India, though Q4 margins were impacted by one-off North launch costs and temporary GGBS supply disruptions at Dolvi. The company maintains a mid-to-high teens volume growth guidance for FY27, underpinned by a robust cost-reduction roadmap targeting INR100/ton savings through green energy adoption and logistics optimization.
